subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - next steps

Thanks for the call this morning, Sam - good alignment overall. Recap + proposed next steps below.

Quick recap of what you shared:
- Primary use case: interactive customer assistant embedded in your web app (multi-turn).
- Latency target: interactive feel, you mentioned aiming for ~p95 <= 300ms for 512-token responses as an initial goal.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected steady-state ~150 RPS with spikes to ~400 RPS during peak; concurrency target ~80 active sessions.
- Streaming: partial token streaming (server push) is required for UX; connection durability during streaming is important.

What we want to validate in the benchmark:
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) measured at request-completion and at first-token/stream-start, for the target sequence-length distribution.
- Throughput under target concurrency (sustained RPS) and tail behavior during burst traffic.
- Stability: cold-start vs warm (after KV-cache warm) and impact of batching.
- Reproducibility: prompt sets, expected outputs, model variant and quantization settings, hardware, and run scripts.

Action items / asks from EdgeFin (please send):
1) Canonical prompt set(s) and representative context distributions (short, medium, long).
2) Any "golden" expected outputs or acceptance criteria you use for quality.
3) Target model versions/quantization you intend to run in production.
4) Preferred test window / staging access (if you want Redwood to run the harness in your staging account).

What we'll provide from Redwood:
- Our benchmark methodology doc and eval harness (standardized, reproducible runs).
- A suggested measurement matrix (p50/p95/p99 latency at request and first-token, tokens/sec throughput, success rate, error types).
- A proposed run schedule and summary report template.

Proposed timeline: if you can share prompt sets & infra specs by end of week, we can schedule an initial run next week and share results within 5 business days.

Thanks - looping in Rishi/Ethan (solutions + infra) to help define measurement details and schedule.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@edgefin.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 13:20:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - next steps

Marissa - thanks for the write-up and clear asks. See attached prompt set + expected outputs for a first pass. A few clarifications inline below.

Attachments:
- edgefin_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt text, category tag, avg_context_tokens)
- edgefin_expected_outputs_v1.json (sample expected replies / acceptance notes)

Clarifications:
- Latency targets: our product team would be comfortable with p95 <= 300ms as a workable bar for interactive flows; if you can show <250ms that's ideal but not a hard requirement for launch.
- Throughput: steady-state 150 RPS looks right; planning for 60-90 concurrency for typical working sets, spike to 400 RPS for marketing events (we expect short bursts ~2-3m).
- Streaming: yes, we stream partial tokens to the client. UX requires first-token streaming under 120ms ideally.
- Model: we'll start with open-model v2.1 (unquantized) for fidelity checks, then test a 4-bit quantized variant for the cost/latency trade.

We don't block you from running tests in our staging account - happy to provide read-only creds scoped to benchmarking. I'll attach our infra spec and expected test window in a follow-up.

Below is our internal note of the prompt categories included: short_instruction, multi_turn_support, long_context_referential.

Best,
Sam Wilson
Director of Product | EdgeFin
sam.wilson@edgefin.com
(415) 555-6789
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology - next steps

Sam - appreciate the prompt set and initial targets. Attaching Redwood's benchmark methodology (v2) so we're aligned on measurement definitions.

Attachment: redwood_benchmark_methodology_v2.pdf

A few measurement clarifications and requests to help reproducibility:
- Measurement points: we report both request-level latency (time from request received to final-token emitted) and first-token latency (time to first byte/token) for streaming flows. We compute p50/p95/p99 over request-level samples. Please confirm which you prefer as primary SLO (we recommend p95 request-level + first-token p95 as complementary).
- Sequence length distribution: include avg and 90th percentile sequence lengths (input + output). We'll use your per-category avg_context_tokens as weights when constructing the run.
- Cold vs warm: we will run a small number of cold-starts (server instance startup and model load) and a warm steady-state window. Please confirm acceptable cold-start window (e.g., <= 5s for model load?).
- Batching & concurrency: please confirm whether you'd accept batching at the gateway and max batch size. If you require strictly single-request processing, note that will materially impact throughput.
- Hardware & model metadata: for reproducibility, provide GPU type, driver/runtime versions, model commit hash (if applicable), quantization config, and any kernel optimizations. We'll include these in the run report.

Operational ask: if you can provide a staging endpoint + read-only creds and a reachable artifact bucket (we can pull prompt sets), we can run the harness from our infra. Otherwise we can provide a self-run package (edgefin_eval_harness.zip) with instructions and a docker image.

Proposed timeline: we can kick off an internal smoke run within 3 business days after we have the prompt set + infra specs and complete a full reproducible run within ~7 business days.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
